general_information.Description: Objective: Students understand the various components that contribute to the design of a tourism product, such as local culture, important holidays, nearby resorts, modes of transportation, the availability of intermediary service providers, and the development prospects of that tourism product in the country's tourism industry's future. Students must generate an idea, create a product, and persuade the class that it is effective, viable, sustainable, and has the potential for development, in which students must present analysis of the strategic products of various organizations using case studies. Description: This course teaches the structure, functions, operations, strategies, and other aspects of tourism goods, as well as how to build and implement one or more comprehensive tourism products. The course also analyzes and provides information on specific tourism items such as specific fascination, cultural, religious, and so forth. The course also includes real-life case studies on tourism product design.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purposes - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online support from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Define and analyze the extent of services, evaluate the relevance of services in the economy as a whole, and tourism services in particular.
Distinguish between the marketing mix for tangible products and the marketing mix for intangible services, and investigate the use of service in tourism.
Understand all of the aspects that drive tourism product ideation, design, and implementation, such as destination selection, culture, entertainment, and so on.
Investigate the processes of tourism product development, from concept design to actual execution, as well as the method of tourism product operation.
Understand several fundamental and unique forms of tourist products, such as cultural, religious, resort, beach, and event types, among others.
Define a communication and promotion strategy to extensively spread typical tourism products and stress the sustainability of tourism products using communication methods.
Analyze and evaluate several organizations' tourism product strategies using common case studies.
Develop products that address contemporary issues in the development of tourist products for events, resorts, cruises, and other tourism products.
Acquire professional attitudes and abilities to obtain an understanding of designing tourism products for a wide range of customers.

assessments.Grading Guide: Participation grade will be given based on students' preparation, and quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and builds upon others’ comments. Class preparation and pre-reading before lecture will be assessed upon individuals' understanding and ability to answer questions in the class. Individuals will be called up randomly to be assessed.

assessments.No Question: Written report: limitation of 4000 words Presentation: 30 mins/group
assessments.Grading Guide: Each group comprises of four to five students who prepare and present to the class a creative and one-of-a-kind tourist product for their travel company. The report must be a synthesis of a creative idea, an academic strategic analysis and a realisticl business plan. Students are encouraged to apply all the knowledge and skills gained from the course to design a tourism product. If the submission product is found to be a product produced/designed by another party, the student will fail this assignment. Students are required to provide written and oral reports.

assessments.CLO: CLO1, CLO2, CLO3, CLO4, CLO6, CLO7, CLO8, CLO9
assessments.Grading Guide: Students will be requested to submit an essay after participating in the Fieldtrip at any local tourist agency to share the knowledge they have acquired, the content of the essay needs to be based on the knowledge students have learned such as concepts, target customer, market analysis, diversity of tourism products, sustainability factors, to conduct an analysis of the tourism products that a company is developing, and comment on the feasibility implementation as well as the likelihood of success of that product. In addition, teachers might ask for extra questions that are relevant to the Fieldtrip.
